title: New Criminal Laws: BNS, BNSS and BSA: Quiz

questions.question: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced which earlier law?
questions.rationale: The BNS is the substantive criminal code replacing the IPC of 1860. The CrPC is replaced by the BNSS and the Evidence Act by the BSA.

questions.question: From which date did the three new criminal laws come into force?
questions.rationale: Parliament passed them on 21 December 2023 and they received assent on 25 December 2023, but they came into force on 1 July 2024.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs the new law with the Act it replaced?
options: BNSS with Code of Criminal Procedure
BSA with Code of Criminal Procedure
BNS with Code of Criminal Procedure
questions.rationale: BNSS replaced the CrPC; the BSA replaced the Indian Evidence Act; the BNS replaced the IPC.

questions.question: Under the BNS, murder is punishable under which section?
questions.rationale: IPC 302 became BNS 103. Section 100 defines culpable homicide, and 111 deals with organised crime.

questions.question: Which of these is a new offence introduced in the BNS, with no direct IPC equivalent?
questions.rationale: Organised crime (Section 111) is new. Theft, cheating and defamation existed in the IPC as 379, 420 and 500.

questions.question: The BNSS has how many sections?
questions.rationale: BNSS has 531 sections in 39 chapters. 358 is the BNS and 170 is the BSA.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about sedition is correct?
options: Sedition was shifted to the BNSS
The BNS has no offence called sedition, but Section 152 punishes acts endangering India's sovereignty, unity and integrity
Section 124A of the IPC was carried over unchanged into the BNS
The BNS raised the punishment for sedition to death
questions.rationale: The BNS drops sedition by name and replaces it with Section 152 on acts endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity.

questions.question: Zero FIR, which allows registration at any police station regardless of jurisdiction, is given statutory recognition in which Act?
questions.rationale: Section 173 of the BNSS recognises Zero FIR; the BNS is about offences and the BSA is about evidence.

questions.question: Which pair of numbers gives the number of sections in the BNS and the BSA respectively?
questions.rationale: BNS has 358 sections, BSA has 170. 531 belongs to the BNSS.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a change associated with the new criminal laws?
options: Abolition of the Supreme Court's power to hear criminal appeals
Terrorism defined as a separate offence in the BNS
Community service as a punishment for some petty offences
Electronic records recognised as documents and primary evidence
questions.rationale: No such abolition was made. The other three are real changes: community service, electronic records in the BSA, and terrorism in BNS Section 113.

questions.question: In the BSA, the certificate for electronic evidence, earlier in Section 65B of the Evidence Act, is found in:
questions.rationale: Section 63 of the BSA corresponds to the old 65B certificate for electronic records.

questions.question: Mob lynching by a group of five or more persons on grounds such as race, caste or language is covered in the BNS under:
questions.rationale: Section 103(2) adds mob lynching as an aggravated murder, with death or life imprisonment. 318 is cheating, 356 defamation and 64 punishment for rape.

questions.question: Cheating, earlier punished under IPC Section 420, is now covered by which BNS section?
questions.rationale: Cheating is BNS 318. Theft is 303, robbery 309 and defamation 356.

questions.question: Which statement about the three laws is correct?
options: The BNSS deals with procedure and has more sections than the BNS
The BNS deals with procedure of arrest
All three have identical numbers of sections
The BSA is the longest of the three
questions.rationale: BNSS (531) has more sections than BNS (358), and BNSS is the procedural code. BNS lists offences.
